reasoning_traces.think:
The Kelly Criterion arises from optimizing long-term wealth growth under repeated binary gambles. It begins with defining a 'favorable game' where capital can grow unboundedly with positive probability. The naive approach of maximizing expected gain leads to ruin due to unbounded betting. Instead, the Kelly rule derives the optimal fraction of capital to bet per trial: f* = p - q, assuming even-money payouts. This balances growth rate maximization with ruin avoidance. The derivation uses logarithmic utility to ensure stability and avoids the pitfalls of linear expectation maximization. In GSI, this maps to Bayesian updating of belief parameters over time series data, while in GSE, it defines a recursive state transition policy for capital allocation across trials.
